tasks.title: Sorn — continuous force versus discrete 4%
tasks.context: A demographer models the population of Sorn by $f(t)=6\,e^{0.04t}$, where $t$ is years after a census and $f(t)$ is measured in millions of residents. A rival analyst proposes replacing the continuous path by annual compounding at nominal rate $4\%$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=12$, the continuous model does not exceed $9.5$ million.
Replacing $e^{0.04t}$ by $(1+0.04)^{t}$ leaves the path unchanged for every $t$.
Over a single year the continuous model multiplies the population by a factor not strictly larger than $1+0.04$.
The continuous doubling time is strictly less than $40$ years.
At $t=12$, the discrete path $g(t)=6(1+0.04)^{t}$ lies not strictly below the continuous path.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Name the growth law that the claim depends on, then substitute the recovered values.

Substitute the recovered force into the continuous level formula.

$$f(12)=6\,e^{0.04\cdot12}$$

$$=6\,e^{0.48}$$

$$\approx9.6964$$

Compare with the claimed threshold $9.5$ million:

$$9.6964 > 9.5$$

The comparison above is exactly what the statement asks, so the statement is True.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.

**B.** → False

Two closed forms agree for all $t$ only when their one-year multipliers match.

$$1+0.04=1.04$$

$$e^{0.04}\approx1.040811$$

Since $1.04\neq e^{0.04}$, the discrete replacement $(1+0.04)^{t}$ is not identical to $e^{0.04t}$. At the concrete horizon $t=12$ the values already differ (9.6062 versus 9.6964).

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Name the growth law that the claim depends on, then substitute the recovered values.

Under continuous force $k$, the exact one-year multiplier is $e^{k}$, not $1+k$.

$$e^{0.04}-1\approx0.040811$$

$$1+0.04=1.04$$

For $k>0$ the inequality $e^{k}>1+k$ holds, so the continuous year-over-year growth factor exceeds $1+0.04$.

$$1.040811 > 1.04$$

Set beside the claim, the recovered figures decide that the statement is True.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Convert the claim into one equation in the shared model and solve it step by step.

Doubling means $f(t)=2f(0)$, which forces $e^{kt}=2$.

$$t=\frac{\ln 2}{0.04}$$

$$t\approx17.3287$$

Compare with $40$:

$$17.3287 < 40$$

The comparison above is exactly what the statement asks, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Name the growth law that the claim depends on, then substitute the recovered values.

The overview already recovered $f(12)\approx9.6964$ and $g(12)\approx9.6062$. Compare those two levels directly:

$$g(12)=6(1+0.04)^{12}\approx9.6062$$

$$f(12)\approx9.6964$$

$$9.6062 < 9.6964$$

The comparison above is exactly what the statement asks, so the statement is True.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.
tasks.solution_overview:
The overview recovers the continuous census model

$$f(t)=6\,e^{0.04t}$$

for Sorn, with $f$ in millions of residents. The continuous annual force is $k=0.04$. At $t=12$,

$$f(12)=6\,e^{0.04\cdot12}\approx9.6964$$

The naive discrete rival $g(t)=6(1+0.04)^{t}$ gives $g(12)\approx9.6062$. One-year continuous growth is $e^{k}-1\approx0.040811$, not the force $k$ itself. Doubling solves $e^{kt}=2$, so $t=\ln 2/k\approx17.3287$.

tasks.title: Frost — GDP per capita force trap
tasks.context: In Frost, aggregate real GDP (billions of dollars) follows $Y(t)=550\,e^{0.04t}$ while population (millions) follows $N(t)=11\,e^{0.018t}$. Analysts track GDP per capita $y=Y/N$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Real GDP per capita grows at continuous annual force different from $0.022$.
After $12$ years, GDP per capita exceeds $1.4$ times its initial level.
Because both GDP and population grow, the per-capita force equals $0.04+0.018$.
The identity $y(t)=Y(t)/N(t)$ holds at $t=12$ for the recovered paths.
Using force $0.04+0.018$ for per capita does not overstate the true $y(12)$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Translate the wording into a threshold comparison against the recovered level.

Take natural logs of the ratio definition.

$$\ln y(t)=\ln Y(t)-\ln N(t)$$

$$=\ln Y_0+gt-(\ln N_0+pt)$$

$$=\ln(Y_0/N_0)+(g-p)t$$

Hence the continuous force on $y$ is exactly $g-p=0.04-0.018=0.022$.

Reading the inequality against the recovered value shows the statement is True.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Read the recovered parameters from the overview and test only this comparison.

The overview recovered $y(12)\approx65.1064$ and $y_0=50$.

$$1.4\,y_0=70$$

$$y(12)=50\,e^{0.022\cdot12}\approx65.1064$$

$$65.1064 \le 70$$

Matching those displays with the wording of the claim gives verdict False.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Name the growth law that the claim depends on, then substitute the recovered values.

Adding the two forces would describe a product $Y\cdot N$, not the ratio $Y/N$.

$$\frac{d}{dt}\ln(Y/N)=g-p=0.022$$

$$g+p=0.058$$

The claim asserts force $0.058$, but the recovered per-capita force is $0.022$. Those are not equal.

The comparison above is exactly what the statement asks, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Read the recovered parameters from the overview and test only this comparison.

Compute the ratio of the recovered aggregate paths and compare with $y(12)$.

$$\frac{Y(12)}{N(12)}=\frac{888.8409}{13.6521}\approx65.1064$$

$$y(12)\approx65.1064$$

The absolute gap is about $0$, which is numerical noise, so the identity holds.

Reading the inequality against the recovered value shows the statement is True.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Read the recovered parameters from the overview and test only this comparison.

The additive-trap path would be

$$y_{\mathrm{wrong}}(t)=50\,e^{(0.04+0.018)t}\approx100.2857$$

while the true level is

$$y(12)\approx65.1064$$

$$100.2857 > 65.1064$$

Matching those displays with the wording of the claim gives verdict True.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Aggregate real GDP (billions) follows $Y(t)=550\,e^{0.04t}$ while population (millions) follows $N(t)=11\,e^{0.018t}$. GDP per capita is the ratio

$$y(t)=\frac{Y(t)}{N(t)}=50\,e^{(0.04-0.018)t}=50\,e^{0.022t}$$

So the continuous per-capita force is the difference $g-p=0.022$, not a sum. At $t=12$:

$$y(12)\approx65.1064,\quad Y(12)\approx888.8409,\quad N(12)\approx13.6521.$$

tasks.title: Orion — piecewise force then solve for $t$
tasks.context: The Orion fund starts at $1000$ and grows continuously at force $0.05$ until $t=6$, then at force $0.01$. A covenant asks when the balance first reaches $1500$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The target level $15000$ is first reached at some time strictly after the rate switch $t=6$.
Ignoring the rate switch and extrapolating force $0.5$ all the way changes the hitting time.
By the switch time $t=6$ the fund has already reached at least $1500$.
The average continuous force on $[0,6]$ recovered from $f(6)/P_0$ equals $0.05$.
Conditional on crossing after the switch, the remaining time does not equal $\ln(1500/f(6))/0.01$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

At the switch, $f(6)\approx1349.8588$. Compare with the target $1500$:

$$1349.8588 < 1500$$

Because the switch level is still below the target and $k_2=0.01>0$, solve

$$f(6)\,e^{0.01(t-6)}=1500$$

$$t=6+\frac{\ln(1500/1349.8588)}{0.01}\approx16.5465$$

Since $16.5465>6$, the first hitting time is after the switch.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Convert the claim into one equation in the shared model and solve it step by step.

Constant-force extrapolation with $k=0.05$ would solve

$$1000\,e^{0.05t}=1500$$

$$t=\frac{\ln(1500/1000)}{0.05}\approx8.1093$$

The piecewise hitting time is $\approx16.5465$. Those times differ, so ignoring the switch changes the answer.

Set beside the claim, the recovered figures decide that the statement is True.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Name the growth law that the claim depends on, then substitute the recovered values.

Evaluate the piecewise path at the switch only.

$$f(6)\approx1349.8588$$

$$1349.8588 < 1500$$

Therefore the claim is False under the shared model.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Translate the wording into a threshold comparison against the recovered level.

On $[0,6]$ the force is constant $k_1$, so

$$\frac{1}{T}\ln\frac{f(6)}{P_0}=\frac{1}{6}\ln\frac{1349.8588}{1000}$$

$$\approx0.05$$

which matches $k_1=0.05$.

Reading the inequality against the recovered value shows the statement is True.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Convert the claim into one equation in the shared model and solve it step by step.

From $f(6)\,e^{k_2(t-T)}=1500$ take logs:

$$k_2(t-T)=\ln\frac{1500}{f(6)}$$

$$t-T=\frac{\ln(1500/f(6))}{0.01}$$

That is exactly the claimed remaining-time formula and applies here.

Therefore the claim is True under the shared model.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview:
The fund starts at $P_0=1000$ and grows with piecewise continuous force $k=0.05$ on $[0,6]$ and $k=0.01$ afterward.

$$f(6)=1000\,e^{0.05\cdot6}\approx1349.8588$$

For $t>6$,

$$f(t)=f(6)\,e^{0.01(t-6)}.$$

Hitting level $1500$ after the switch solves $t=6+\ln(1500/f(6))/0.01$ $\approx16.5465$.

tasks.title: Sample-A — half-life decay
tasks.context: A lab sample of mass $m_0=64$ grams of Sample-A decays with half-life $T_{1/2}=6$ hours under $m(t)=m_0 e^{-kt}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: After $18$ hours the remaining mass is not strictly less than $15$ grams.
The continuous decay constant does not equal $\ln 2/6$.
After $180$ hours the sample retains exactly one eighth of its initial mass.
After $18$ hours more than $6$ grams remain.
The mass falls below $6$ grams at some time strictly before $t=18$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Convert the claim into one equation in the shared model and solve it step by step.

Count half-lives and apply the geometric decay formula.

$$\frac{18}{6}=3$$

$$m(18)=64\cdot\left(\tfrac12\right)^{3}=8$$

$$8 < 15$$

Set beside the claim, the recovered figures decide that the statement is True.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Translate the wording into a threshold comparison against the recovered level.

By definition of half-life under $m(t)=m_0 e^{-kt}$,

$$m(T_{1/2})=\tfrac12 m_0\implies e^{-k T_{1/2}}=\tfrac12$$

$$k=\frac{\ln 2}{T_{1/2}}=\frac{\ln 2}{6}\approx0.115525.$$

The claim matches that identity.

Set beside the claim, the recovered figures decide that the statement is True.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Name the growth law that the claim depends on, then substitute the recovered values.

One eighth remains after exactly three half-lives. Here

$$\frac{t}{T_{1/2}}=3$$

and $m_0/8=8$. The actual remainder is $8$, so the claim is correct.

The comparison above is exactly what the statement asks, so the statement is True.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.

**D.** → True

Keep the continuous-versus-discrete distinction explicit while checking the claim.

From the overview, $m(18)=8$. Compare with $6$:

$$8 > 6$$

Reading the inequality against the recovered value shows the statement is True.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → False

Translate the wording into a threshold comparison against the recovered level.

Solve $m(t)=6$ under the recovered $k$.

$$64\,e^{-kt}=6$$

$$t=\frac{\ln(64/6)}{k}\approx20.4902$$

$$20.4902 \ge 18$$

Reading the inequality against the recovered value shows the statement is False.

So the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Half-life $T_{1/2}=6$ forces continuous decay constant

$$k=\frac{\ln 2}{6}\approx0.115525$$

and

$$m(t)=64\,e^{-kt}=64\left(\tfrac12\right)^{t/6}.$$

At $t=18$, the sample has lived $3$ half-lives, so $m(18)=8$.

tasks.title: Newton cooling — ambient trap
tasks.context: A cup cools under Newton's law $T(t)=T_a+(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}$ with $T_0=75$, ambient $T_a=15$, and $k=0.045$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=35$ the temperature is not strictly below $30$.
At $t=35$ the temperature remains not strictly above ambient $T_a=15$.
As $t\to\infty$ the model temperature approaches the initial temperature $T_0$.
The temperature reaches $30$ at some time strictly before $t=35$.
The deviation from ambient at $t=35$ equals $(T_0-T_a)e^{-0.045\cdot35}$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Name the growth law that the claim depends on, then substitute the recovered values.

Substitute into Newton's law.

$$T(35)=15+(60)e^{-1.575}$$

$$\approx27.4205$$

$$27.4205 < 30$$

Set beside the claim, the recovered figures decide that the statement is True.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.

So the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Convert the claim into one equation in the shared model and solve it step by step.

Because $e^{-kt}\in(0,1)$ for finite $t>0$ and $T_0>T_a$,

$$T(t)-T_a=(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}>0.$$

Numerically $T(35)\approx27.4205>15$.

Reading the inequality against the recovered value shows the statement is True.

The wording of the claim was flipped relative to that comparison, so the same recovered numbers now make the statement False.

So the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Read the recovered parameters from the overview and test only this comparison.

The long-run limit of Newton's law is the ambient temperature, not $T_0$:

$$\lim_{t\to\infty}T(t)=T_a=15.$$

The claim that the limit equals $T_0=75$ is false.

Therefore the claim is False under the shared model.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Convert the claim into one equation in the shared model and solve it step by step.

Solve $T(t)=30$:

$$t=-\frac{1}{k}\ln\frac{30-15}{75-15}\approx30.8065$$

$$30.8065 < 35$$

The comparison above is exactly what the statement asks, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Translate the wording into a threshold comparison against the recovered level.

Rearrange the model:

$$T(t)-T_a=(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}.$$

At $t=35$ the right-hand side equals $12.4205$, matching $T(35)-T_a$.

Set beside the claim, the recovered figures decide that the statement is True.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:
Newton cooling: $T(t)=T_a+(T_0-T_a)e^{-kt}$ with $T_0=75$, $T_a=15$, $k=0.045$.

$$T(35)=15+(75-15)e^{-0.045\cdot35}\approx27.4205.$$

Time to reach $30$ solves $t=-\ln\frac{30-T_a}{T_0-T_a}/k\approx30.8065$.

tasks.context: In Boreal, aggregate real GDP (billions of dollars) follows $Y(t)=400\,e^{0.025t}$ while population (millions) follows $N(t)=8\,e^{0.008t}$. Analysts track GDP per capita $y=Y/N$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Real GDP per capita grows at continuous annual force exactly $0.017$.

**A.** → True

Keep the continuous-versus-discrete distinction explicit while checking the claim.

Take natural logs of the ratio definition.

$$\ln y(t)=\ln Y(t)-\ln N(t)$$

$$=\ln Y_0+gt-(\ln N_0+pt)$$

$$=\ln(Y_0/N_0)+(g-p)t$$

Hence the continuous force on $y$ is exactly $g-p=0.025-0.008=0.017$.

Matching those displays with the wording of the claim gives verdict True.

So the statement is True.

The comparison above is exactly what the statement asks, so the statement is False.

Therefore the claim is False under the shared model.

So the statement is False.

Matching those displays with the wording of the claim gives verdict True.

So the statement is True.

$$90.5609 > 67.8991$$

Therefore the claim is True under the shared model.

So the statement is True.

tasks.context: The Polar fund starts at $2000$ and grows continuously at force $0.04$ until $t=5$, then at force $0.02$. A covenant asks when the balance first reaches $2800$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The target level $2800$ is first reached at some time strictly after the rate switch $t=5$.
Ignoring the rate switch and extrapolating force $0.04$ all the way changes the hitting time.
By the switch time $t=5$ the fund has already reached at least $2800$.
The average continuous force on $[0,5]$ recovered from $f(5)/P_0$ equals $0.04$.
Conditional on crossing after the switch, the remaining time equals $\ln(2800/f(5))/0.02$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

At the switch, $f(5)\approx2442.8055$. Compare with the target $2800$:

$$2442.8055 < 2800$$

Because the switch level is still below the target and $k_2=0.02>0$, solve

$$f(5)\,e^{0.02(t-5)}=2800$$

$$t=5+\frac{\ln(2800/2442.8055)}{0.02}\approx11.8236$$

Since $11.8236>5$, the first hitting time is after the switch.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Read the recovered parameters from the overview and test only this comparison.

Constant-force extrapolation with $k=0.04$ would solve

$$2000\,e^{0.04t}=2800$$

$$t=\frac{\ln(2800/2000)}{0.04}\approx8.4118$$

The piecewise hitting time is $\approx11.8236$. Those times differ, so ignoring the switch changes the answer.

Set beside the claim, the recovered figures decide that the statement is True.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Keep the continuous-versus-discrete distinction explicit while checking the claim.

Evaluate the piecewise path at the switch only.

$$f(5)\approx2442.8055$$

$$2442.8055 < 2800$$

Reading the inequality against the recovered value shows the statement is False.

So the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Read the recovered parameters from the overview and test only this comparison.

On $[0,5]$ the force is constant $k_1$, so

$$\frac{1}{T}\ln\frac{f(5)}{P_0}=\frac{1}{5}\ln\frac{2442.8055}{2000}$$

$$\approx0.04$$

which matches $k_1=0.04$.

Therefore the claim is True under the shared model.

So the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Read the recovered parameters from the overview and test only this comparison.

From $f(5)\,e^{k_2(t-T)}=2800$ take logs:

$$k_2(t-T)=\ln\frac{2800}{f(5)}$$

$$t-T=\frac{\ln(2800/f(5))}{0.02}$$

$$f(5)=2000\,e^{0.04\cdot5}\approx2442.8055$$

For $t>5$,

$$f(t)=f(5)\,e^{0.02(t-5)}.$$

tasks.title: Lysova — continuous force versus discrete 2%
tasks.context: A demographer models the population of Lysova by $f(t)=10\,e^{0.02t}$, where $t$ is years after a census and $f(t)$ is measured in millions of residents. A rival analyst proposes replacing the continuous path by annual compounding at nominal rate $2\%$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=25$, the continuous model exceeds $16$ million.
Replacing $e^{0.02t}$ by $(1+0.02)^{t}$ leaves the path unchanged for every $t$.
Over a single year the continuous model multiplies the population by a factor strictly larger than $1+0.02$.
The continuous doubling time is strictly less than $40$ years.
At $t=25$, the discrete path $g(t)=10(1+0.02)^{t}$ lies strictly below the continuous path.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Read the recovered parameters from the overview and test only this comparison.

Substitute the recovered force into the continuous level formula.

$$f(25)=10\,e^{0.02\cdot25}$$

$$=10\,e^{0.5}$$

$$\approx16.4872$$

Compare with the claimed threshold $16$ million:

$$16.4872 > 16$$

Reading the inequality against the recovered value shows the statement is True.

So the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Two closed forms agree for all $t$ only when their one-year multipliers match.

$$1+0.02=1.02$$

$$e^{0.02}\approx1.020201$$

Since $1.02\neq e^{0.02}$, the discrete replacement $(1+0.02)^{t}$ is not identical to $e^{0.02t}$. At the concrete horizon $t=25$ the values already differ (16.4061 versus 16.4872).

So the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Keep the continuous-versus-discrete distinction explicit while checking the claim.

Under continuous force $k$, the exact one-year multiplier is $e^{k}$, not $1+k$.

$$e^{0.02}-1\approx0.020201$$

$$1+0.02=1.02$$

For $k>0$ the inequality $e^{k}>1+k$ holds, so the continuous year-over-year growth factor exceeds $1+0.02$.

$$1.020201 > 1.02$$

Set beside the claim, the recovered figures decide that the statement is True.

So the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Convert the claim into one equation in the shared model and solve it step by step.

Doubling means $f(t)=2f(0)$, which forces $e^{kt}=2$.

$$t=\frac{\ln 2}{0.02}$$

$$t\approx34.6574$$

Compare with $40$:

$$34.6574 < 40$$

The comparison above is exactly what the statement asks, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Name the growth law that the claim depends on, then substitute the recovered values.

The overview already recovered $f(25)\approx16.4872$ and $g(25)\approx16.4061$. Compare those two levels directly:

$$g(25)=10(1+0.02)^{25}\approx16.4061$$

$$f(25)\approx16.4872$$

$$16.4061 < 16.4872$$

Set beside the claim, the recovered figures decide that the statement is True.

So the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview:
The overview recovers the continuous census model

$$f(t)=10\,e^{0.02t}$$

for Lysova, with $f$ in millions of residents. The continuous annual force is $k=0.02$. At $t=25$,

$$f(25)=10\,e^{0.02\cdot25}\approx16.4872$$

The naive discrete rival $g(t)=10(1+0.02)^{t}$ gives $g(25)\approx16.4061$. One-year continuous growth is $e^{k}-1\approx0.020201$, not the force $k$ itself. Doubling solves $e^{kt}=2$, so $t=\ln 2/k\approx34.6574$.

tasks.title: Competing continuous and discrete forecasts
tasks.context: Two forecasts start at $80$: continuous $f(t)=80\,e^{0.06t}$ and discrete $g(t)=80\,(1.055)^{t}$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At $t=5$ the continuous model exceeds the discrete base-$1.055$ model.
The continuous force $0.06$ exceeds $\ln(1.055)$.
At $t=5$ the two models differ by less than $5\%$ relative to the larger value.
The continuous model doubles strictly sooner than the discrete model.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Keep the continuous-versus-discrete distinction explicit while checking the claim.

Read the two terminal levels from the overview (or the figure).

$$f(5)\approx107.9887$$

$$g(5)\approx104.5568$$

$$107.9887 > 104.5568$$

The comparison above is exactly what the statement asks, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Name the growth law that the claim depends on, then substitute the recovered values.

Compute the discrete force and compare with $k$.

$$\ln(1.055)\approx0.053541$$

$$0.06 > 0.053541$$

Matching those displays with the wording of the claim gives verdict True.

So the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Convert the claim into one equation in the shared model and solve it step by step.

Relative gap against the larger level:

$$\frac{|f-g|}{\max(f,g)}\approx0.03178$$

$$0.03178 < 0.05$$

The comparison above is exactly what the statement asks, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Convert the claim into one equation in the shared model and solve it step by step.

$$t_{\mathrm{cont}}=\frac{\ln 2}{0.06}\approx11.5525$$

$$t_{\mathrm{disc}}=\frac{\ln 2}{\ln(1.055)}\approx12.9462$$

$$11.5525 < 12.9462$$

The comparison above is exactly what the statement asks, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Translate the wording into a threshold comparison against the recovered level.

Algebraically,

$$\ln\frac{Pe^{kt}}{P a^{t}}=(k-\ln a)t$$

$$=(0.06-0.053541)\cdot5\approx0.032296.$$

Direct evaluation of $\ln(f/g)$ recovers the same number, so the identity holds.

Therefore the claim is True under the shared model.

So the statement is True.
